findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. Since `isTeamOwner` is a strict subset of `isTeamAdmin` (an OWNER role satisfies both, but an ADMIN-only role satisfies only `isTeamAdmin`), this expression is effectively equivalent to just `isTeamOwner`. As a result, a team ADMIN who is not also the OWNER, and who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee, will be incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team member's booking, even though team admins should normally have this privilege (as elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. reassign). This should be `||`.

findings.title: EventManager built with requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches credentials for the user making the request, and `EventManager` is instantiated with `{ ...user, credentials }` where `user` is `ctx.user`. Because the permission check above allows an attendee (not just the organizer) to add guests, when an attendee triggers this flow the calendar sync in `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the attendee's own (likely absent or unrelated) calendar credentials rather than the organizer's. The booking already fetched `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }` (the organizer), but those credentials are never used. This can silently fail to update the organizer's actual calendar event with the new guests.

findings.title: Guest email blacklist comparison is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is built by lower-casing every entry from `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, but the comparison `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` uses the raw, non-lowercased `guest` value. A blocked email such as `spam@example.com` can bypass the blacklist simply by submitting `Spam@Example.com` or `SPAM@EXAMPLE.COM`, since the exact-case string will never match the lowercased blacklist entries.

findings.title: Duplicate-guest detection is case-sensitive
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` is derived by checking `guest === attendee.email` without normalizing case. Combined with the client-side uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (which also does a case-sensitive `Set` comparison), a guest can be added twice with differing email casing (e.g. `John@Example.com` vs `john@example.com`), creating duplicate Attendee rows that represent the same real email address and causing duplicate notifications/calendar invites for what is effectively the same guest.

findings.title: Wrong attendee email template sent when a resubmitted guest email is not actually new
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` decides which template to send an attendee based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. The caller (`addGuests.handler.ts`, line 168) passes the raw, unfiltered `guests` array from the request rather than `uniqueGuests` (the guests that were actually inserted after filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted emails). If a user resubmits an email that is already an existing attendee (so it gets filtered out of `uniqueGuests` and not re-added to the DB), that existing attendee's email is still present in `guests`, causing them to incorrectly receive the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (meant for brand-new attendees) instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, which is confusing and semantically wrong.

findings.title: Email-send failure is swallowed with a bare console.log, losing error details
findings.body: The `catch (err)` block around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only logs the static string `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` via `console.log`, discarding the actual `err` object and bypassing the project's structured logger (`@calcom/lib/logger`) used elsewhere in this same file's imports. This makes it impossible to diagnose production email failures for this flow, and `console.log` (rather than `console.error`/the logger) is inconsistent with how errors are handled elsewhere in the codebase.

findings.title: No check on booking status before adding guests
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking and immediately proceeds to add attendees, sync the calendar and send notification emails without verifying `booking.status`. Guests can therefore be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, resulting in calendar invites and "guests added" notification emails being sent for an event that is not actually happening, confusing invitees and polluting calendars with stale events.

findings.title: Fallback toast message in onError is dead code
findings.body: `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` uses `message` which is built from a template literal (`` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` ``) and is therefore always a non-empty, truthy string even when `err.data` or `err.message` are undefined (yielding something like "undefined: undefined"). The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never actually trigger, so users may see a raw/unhelpful "undefined: ..." message instead of the intended friendly error text for unexpected error shapes.

findings.title: isInvalidEmail state is never reset after a successful submission or new attempt
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. If a user triggers the "emails must be unique and valid" error once, then fixes the input and successfully submits (via `handleAdd`'s success branch or the mutation's `onSuccess`), `isInvalidEmail` remains `true`. Since the dialog closes on success but the flag is never cleared, reopening the dialog afterward will immediately show the stale invalid-email warning banner even though no new validation error has occurred.

findings.title: Hardcoded, non-localized tooltip text
findings.body: The remove-email tooltip uses a hardcoded English string `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` instead of going through the `t()` translation function that is already imported and used elsewhere in this same component (e.g. for "add_another" and the field label). This breaks localization for non-English users of this new shared UI component.

findings.title: No automated tests for the new add-guests feature
findings.body: This PR introduces a new tRPC mutation with non-trivial authorization logic (organizer/attendee/team-admin checks), guest deduplication/blacklist filtering, calendar sync, and dual email notifications, plus new UI components (`AddGuestsDialog`, `MultiEmail`). No unit, integration, or component tests are included for any of `addGuests.handler.ts`, `addGuests.schema.ts`, `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, or `MultiEmail.tsx`, despite the permission-check bug and case-sensitivity issues that tests would likely have caught.
